HSTU uses pointwise SiLU attention rather than softmax. In the public research implementation, pre-layer-normalized inputs undergo a fused UVQK projection and configurable SiLU activation. Attention is A = [SiLU(QKᵀ + relative_bias)/N] ⊙ M, followed by AV: N is the padded attention width, not the number of allowed keys. Despite its name, `invalid_attn_mask` is an allow-mask: 1 permits attention; causal validity includes the diagonal. Relative bias adds learned position-offset and bucketed timestamp terms before SiLU. The standard residual update is X + output_projection(dropout(U ⊙ LayerNorm(AV))). See the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) and [reference implementation](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py).

An intervention derived from these semantics should multiply every layer’s post-SiLU attention weights by a broadcast key-column gate: M′[b,i,j] = M[b,i,j] · valid[b,j] · (1 − blocked[b,j]). Preserve slots, timestamps, positional offsets, N and residuals; never compact histories or renormalize over surviving keys. Zeroing K alone is insufficient because relative bias can produce nonzero weights. For left padding, retain the final nonpadding readout. Exclude that slot from blocking: its item embedding survives through its residual and query/gate paths.

Proposed correctness tests, not reported experimental findings: in evaluation mode, compare the original forward pass with an empty intervention; require identical outputs or tight numerical agreement. With blocking active, arbitrarily perturb only blocked input-embedding occurrences and verify unchanged readout features and fixed-candidate scores across multiple layers. Autograd should yield zero readout Jacobian with respect to those occurrences; an unblocked perturbation provides a sensitivity control. Hold candidate embeddings fixed when testing tied embedding tables. Also test future-token invariance and varying left-padding lengths.
